Title: Our On-Call Handover Step
Detail_lesson: Our on-call handover checklist carries this step, word for word: 'Outgoing engineer summarises any open incidents and hands over context to the incoming engineer at the start of the shift.' That is the whole step, and it has been the whole step since the checklist was written. Rewrite it. Give the exact words that go in its place - the same length or shorter - so that two engineers who have never met can complete a handover from the text alone, at any hour, with nobody available to ask.

Title: Our Definition of Done
Detail_lesson: Our definition of done reads, in full: 'Code is merged, tests pass, and the change is documented.' Those eleven words have settled no argument yet - every dispute this team has had about whether something was finished is compatible with all three clauses. Write the replacement. Keep the shape (a short list a reviewer can check off) and make every item something two people would agree on without a conversation.

Title: The Line in the Review Guide Nobody Follows
Detail_lesson: Our code review guide contains this sentence: 'Reviewers should aim to respond to review requests in a timely manner.' It has been there since the guide was written and nothing has ever been measured against it. Replace it with wording a reviewer could actually be held to and would not resent - the sentence itself, including any number you want inside it.

Title: What Our Decision Records Ask For
Detail_lesson: The template for our architecture decision records has a section headed Alternatives Considered, and the instruction under that heading reads: 'List other options that were evaluated.' What comes back is a list of names with no reasons attached, on almost every record we have. Rewrite the instruction - the words that sit under that heading in the template - so that what gets written is what somebody rereading the decision in two years actually needs.

Title: The Line We Put in Front of Customers
Detail_lesson: The sentence at the top of our team page reads: 'We build scalable, reliable platforms that enable our partners to deliver value faster.' Every word of that could be said by any team in this company. Write the sentence that replaces it. Same length or shorter, and it has to be a sentence no other team here could truthfully use.
